label: lem:charpoly-roots-are-eigenvalues
title: Roots of the characteristic polynomial are eigenvalues, over $\mathbb{C}$
statement: Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional vector space over $\mathbb{C}$ and let $f : V \to_{\ell} V$.  Then for every $\lambda \in \mathbb{C}$ in $f.\mathrm{charpoly}.\mathrm{roots}$, $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of $f$.
proof:
Membership in \verb|Polynomial.roots| unfolds via \verb|Polynomial.mem_roots| to ``polynomial is nonzero and $\lambda$ is a root''.  Nonzeroness of $f.\mathrm{charpoly}$ is immediate: by \verb|LinearMap.charpoly_monic| the characteristic polynomial is monic, and a monic polynomial is nonzero (\verb|Polynomial.Monic.ne_zero|, i.e.\ the \verb|.ne_zero| projection of \verb|LinearMap.charpoly_monic|).  This is unconditional --- we do not need $V$ to be nontrivial.

  Now we apply \verb|Module.End.hasEigenvalue_iff_isRoot_charpoly| (the equivalence between eigenvalues and roots of the characteristic polynomial, valid over an integral domain such as $\mathbb{C}$).  This lemma requires \verb|Module.Free| and \verb|Module.Finite| instances on $V$ over $\mathbb{C}$; both are derivable from \verb|FiniteDimensional ℂ V|: a finite-dimensional vector space over a field is automatically free (\verb|Module.Free| via \verb|Module.Free.of_basis|) and finite (\verb|Module.Finite.of_finite|), with the typeclass instances supplied by Mathlib.
